narrative:
The model determined that you have a 58% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability is above the approval threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were the status of your checking account, the property you own, and your installment rate as a percentage of disposable income. 

Your checking account being in negative balance (<0 DM) was the strongest factor pushing the prediction toward bad credit risk. Among approved applicants, only 12.6% have a negative balance, while 59.2% have no checking account at all. This made the model considerably less confident in your application.

The fact that you have no recorded property (unknown/none) was the second most important driver and also increased the likelihood of being seen as higher risk. Only 7.8% of approved applicants fall into this category.

Your installment rate of 2% of disposable income worked in your favor and pushed the prediction toward good credit, as it is lower than the 2.99% average among those who were approved. Unfortunately, these positive aspects were not enough to outweigh the concerns raised by your checking account status and lack of property.

You should focus on building a positive checking account balance and acquiring some form of property or collateral before reapplying. Improving these two areas will have the biggest impact on future decisions.
